summary: Forest Service steel fire tower on Big Stamp Bald, Clay/Cherokee Counties NC; removed in the 1960s, with footings, cistern and storm shelter reported there in 2018.

facts.design: A 30-foot steel tower with a 14 x 14 observation cab
facts.status_note: Removed in the 1960s; the register says concrete footers, a water cistern and an underground storm shelter remained in 2018

visit.trail_note: The Forest Service lists the Big Stamp Trail (TR520) for hiking on the Tusquitee Ranger District; its listing does not describe the lookout site

events.note: Last fire warden Glen Beaver called in the final fire, burning near Tipton, NC, from the tower; the register gives only 'the 1960s', so 1960 stands for the decade
Register field reads 'Removed 1960s'; only the decade is given, so 1960 stands for the decade

evidence.supports: Forest Service tower constructed after the location was deemed useful for fire observation; no construction year given
evidence.quote: Eventually, the location was deemed useful for fire observation and a U.S. Forest Service fire tower was constructed.

evidence.supports: Big Stamp Bald as a seasonal meeting place for two Native American tribes, per Forest Service resources
evidence.quote: seasonal meeting place for two Native American tribes in pre-European times

evidence.supports: last fire warden Glen Beaver called in the final fire near Tipton from the tower, in the 1960s
evidence.quote: The last fire warden, Glen Beaver, called in the final fire, burning near Tipton, North Carolina, from the tower in the 1960s.

evidence.supports: as of 2018 concrete footers, water cistern and underground storm shelter remain at the site
evidence.quote: As of 2018, concrete footers, a water cistern, and underground storm shelter remain at the site.

evidence.supports: 30-foot steel tower with a 14 x 14 observation cab
evidence.quote: A 30-foot steel tower with a 14 x 14 observation cab.

evidence.supports: Cherokee and Clay Counties, Nantahala National Forest
Big Stamp Trail listed for hiking, trail number TR520
trail listed under the Tusquitee Ranger District

corrections.why: The register gives only 'Removed 1960s' and the final fire 'in the 1960s'; no single year is stated, so 1960 should be marked as a decade.

sources.title: Big Stamp Trail
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, National Forests in North Carolina

notes_for_editor: No source gives a construction year, so the story has no built date. Removal and the final fire are dated only to the decade; 1960 in the events is a decade marker. Access is not described by any source, so no access level is recorded. The FFLOS page's footings photo (credit Victoria Oliver) was not added as a photo; its license was not checked. The Forest Service trail listing does not say whether the trail reaches the site.
